messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected on /v1/embeddings (embed-large-v1) in prod-us-east. 5xx spike started ~10:23 UTC, traffic drop for some customers. Alert: errors.p50 > 3% for 10m. Incident: INC-2026
Mira: Acknowledging. I'm on it. pinging @Jordan @Sam for infra/runtime context. :eyes: 
Jordan: I see the grafana spike too — http://grafana.redwood.prod/d/embeddings/embeddings?panelId=5&from=now-15m&to=now — errors are mostly 500 with body "dimension mismatch" and some 429s. Attaching sample logs from the serving runtime.
Sam: grabbing recent deploys... I pushed a batching change to embeddings runtime yesterday (optimize continuous batching) but it rolled out canary->stable at 03:00 UTC. Could be related. rolling back canary? also checking autoscaler events.
Mira: Jordan, can you paste a representative log line? want to confirm error message shape.
Jordan: paste:
```
2026-08-17T10:24:12.341Z ERROR embeddings-handler request_id=req_8a7 dim_check_failed expected=1536 got=1538 model=embed-large-v1 tenant=acct-8923
stack: DimensionMismatchError: expected 1536 vector length
 at validateVectors (/opt/runtime/handlers/embeddings.js:212:19)
```
Mira: ok so the runtime is rejecting some batches because vectors are different lengths. That would explain partial errors if batching mixes requests from clients with different model configs.
Kai: Noted. Do we have per-tenant model binding? I thought we tag requests with model dims at ingress.
Sam: There was a change in batching that removed strict per-request shape checks to improve throughput; it relied on the load-balancer to route homogeneous traffic. Looks like we are seeing cross-tenant mixing during bursts.
Mira: Impact: some requests 500 with dimension mismatch, others succeed. Customers using embeddings at high concurrency may see partial failures and retries -> latency + higher cost.
support-bot: Ticket INC-2026 created. Affected customers: acct-8923, acct-7710, acct-1140. Support summary: "embedding requests intermittently 500 with dimension mismatch". CS alerted.
Jordan: Quick repro: curl against prod edge with two different payloads in parallel. Example:
```
# vector length 1536 (correct)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.prod/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["hello world"]}'

# client with custom model or smaller vector length -> simulate 1538
# (we usually derive dim from model metadata, but clients can send embeddings to a user index)
```
When we force concurrent requests from two simulated tenants, some requests in the batch get validated and others fail.
Mira: Mitigation options:
- Fast: disable new batching behavior and revert to previous per-request validation path (downtime-free config flip). (Sam)
- Medium: re-enable strict per-request dimension checks at ingress to reject mismatched sizes before batching.
- Long: make batching safely multi-tenanted (partition by tenant/model dim) + add tests.
Sam: I'm preparing a rollback patch to re-enable per-request batching isolation. Deploying a config flip to stable pool now. Will post the rollout ID.
Jordan: Adding a temporary WAF-style rule at the LB to tag requests that declare model=embed-large-v1 and queue them separately so the runtime doesn't intermix. But that needs a tiny routing change.
Mira: Prioritizing rollback first. Kai, can you hold on any autoscaler changes? We don't want pods cycling during rollback.
Kai: holding. I've also pinned the dedicated pools for embed-large-v1 to avoid mixed hosts.
Sam: Rolling back batching change — flip: `rc=rollback-emb-batching-2026-08-17` -> started. Will monitor metrics.
deploy-bot: Rollout rollback-emb-batching-2026-08: STARTED by Sam at 10:35 UTC. 3/6 canaries passed.
Mira: Noting that customers who saw failures might have retried; some reported increased token costs. Support to follow up for credits if necessary.
support-bot: Noted. I'll create customer incidents on the listed accounts and advise best-effort mitigation steps (retry with exponential backoff).
Sam: Rollout: 6/6 stable nodes now with rollback. deploy-bot: Rollout rollback-emb-batching-2026-08: COMPLETED at 10:42 UTC
Jordan: Stats look better. Errors down to baseline ~0.05%. p50 latency back to normal. Grafana: http://grafana.redwood.prod/d/embeddings/embeddings?from=now-30m
Mira: Can folks confirm that dimension mismatch errors are no longer appearing in logs? Jordan, any stray errors?
Jordan: Last seen at 10:38; none after 10:40. Sample tail:
```
2026-08-17T10:39:58.112Z INFO embeddings-handler request_id=req_a9b model=embed-large-v1 tenant=acct-8923 processed=ok
```
Mira: Great. Escalation summary for INC-2026:
- Trigger: runtime batching change removed strict per-request validation and allowed mixed-dimension requests to co-batch.
- Symptom: intermittent 500s with "DimensionMismatchError" affecting multiple tenants during bursts.
- Impact: partial outages for embeddings for several customers, increased retries and latency.
- Mitigation: rollback batching change to restore per-request isolation (completed 10:42 UTC).
- Next actions: implement routing partitioning by tenant/model dims, add canary tests that simulate multi-tenant concurrent loads, add alert for dimension-mismatch > 0.1%.

Mira: Also assigning action items:
- Sam: design and deploy a safe multi-tenant batching scheme or revert permanently (owner). (due EOD Tue)
- Jordan: add an alert + dashboards for dim-mismatch and batch composition (owner). (due EOD Mon)
- Kai: update autoscaler and pool pinning docs so we don't mix model shapes during deployments (owner). (due EOW)
- support: contact impacted customers with timeline + credit offer (owner: support-bot / Liz). (ASAP)

Liz: I'll draft customer comms now. Thanks for fast rollback. Will loop in account reps.
Mira: Leaving follow-up postmortem; tagging @product + @research for FYI on model dims. Closing pager. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: PAGER: Incident INC-2026 resolved at 10:44 UTC. Root cause identified. Postmortem scheduled.
Jordan: adding logs and snippets to the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026
Mira: Thanks team. I'll open the incident doc and add timeline. Good job, quick response. :clap:
